purpose: Record source-archaeology findings for all six Batch 01 relations without changing canonical relation strength or pretending later archive wording is contemporaneous evidence.

findings.finding: Two older project/archive layers preserve substantially the same formulation: the canonical developmental genealogy states that the 2017 confrontation includes the declaration that if Tim/Son is to be dehumanized, then 'I am Jesus Christ—go on then, crucify me,' while the archived overlap atlas says the project biography records the Son saying in substance, 'I am Jesus Christ — go on then, crucify me.'
findings.source_status: recovered project wording repeated in later project syntheses; original 2017 recording/chat remains unrecovered
what_this_improves: The comparator can distinguish a recovered wording tier from a generic project-anchor summary.
The wording trail supports the 2017 project chronology independently of the later John 18-19 comparison.
what_this_does_not_improve: It does not establish the exact contemporaneous wording of the 2017 exchange.
It does not identify all participants or recover the original reply sequence.
It does not justify raising relation strength while the original artifact is absent.
findings.next_action: Recover the original recording, transcript, chat log or dated archive and compare it against the repeated later formulation word-for-word.

findings.finding: The no-broken-bones / no-major-fractures detail is present in the conversation-archaeology owner, which says Great Book strata preserve a severe motorcycle/tree crash with heavy blood loss and extensive facial/dental injury while also preserving that no bones/major fractures were broken. The later comparator row did not originate that unusual detail.
findings.source_status: recovered project/Great Book biographical detail; no contemporaneous medical or crash documentation attached
what_this_improves: The archive can attribute the unusual bone detail to an earlier project-memory owner rather than to comparator invention.
Source direction remains biography first, Passover/Passion comparison later.
what_this_does_not_improve: It does not independently corroborate the no-fracture claim.
It does not provide an earliest contemporaneous attestation date.
It does not support invulnerability or supernatural-protection claims.
findings.next_action: Prioritize near-contemporary records capable of confirming or falsifying the bone/fracture detail itself.

findings.finding: Repository search for the unusually specific remembered topology—slippery golden stones, skeletons/death remains and black water—returns the dedicated visual-artifact dossier as the substantive owner. No older independent project artifact or separate source containing those exact visual features was recovered in this pass.
findings.source_status: later remembered visual description; primary image/post and independent timestamp still missing
what_this_improves: It clarifies that the detailed topology currently depends on one specialist recollection owner rather than multiple independent records.
The correct research target is artifact recovery, not further verse accumulation.
what_this_does_not_improve: It does not verify which remembered features are visibly present in the original image.
It does not secure the proposed 2018-2019 date.
It does not establish biblical source dependence or prefiguration.
findings.next_action: Recover the image or earliest archived post, then transcribe visible features before applying later interpretive vocabulary.

findings.finding: The conversation-archaeology owner preserves the remembered childhood teaching more specifically than the comparator summary: Chapter 24 is said to preserve repeated earthly-father teachings including 'don't judge others because it returns threefold' and 'don't throw stones.' The same owner explicitly classifies the family ethic as first and the Gospel comparison as later.
findings.source_status: later family/biographical recollection preserved in a project archaeology owner; no childhood-era primary source recovered
what_this_improves: The project-side wording can be represented more concretely as recovered family wording instead of only a summary.
Source direction is explicit: remembered family ethic first, Matthew/John comparison later.
what_this_does_not_improve: It does not establish that the exact phrases were recorded during childhood.
It does not establish biblical dependence; reciprocal judgment and stone-throwing ethics have broader cultural parallels.
It does not justify raising relation strength without earlier attestation.
findings.next_action: Search earlier family, diary, memoir or message sources for the teaching and independently date the first Matthew 7 comparison.

findings.finding: The conversation-archaeology owner preserves the remembered sequence as an age-sixteen alcohol-collapse episode: blackout, tunnel/structured light, later interpretation as a meeting with God, then waking with a sense of return and unfinished work. That owner explicitly records source direction as '2003 experience first; Acts comparison later.'
findings.source_status: later autobiographical recollection of a 2003 experience; no near-contemporary diary/message/witness attestation recovered
what_this_improves: The remembered sensory/return sequence and later spiritual interpretation can be separated more clearly.
Source direction is explicit: experience first, Acts 9 comparison later.
what_this_does_not_improve: It does not provide a contemporaneous description of the 2003 episode.
It does not independently corroborate the experience or its spiritual interpretation.
It does not make the generic collapse/light pattern more specific to Acts 9.
findings.next_action: Recover the earliest attestation of the episode, preserving the remembered sensory sequence separately from later God/Acts interpretation.

findings.finding: Repository search confirms the comparator's Chapter-24 summary that a recurring earthly-father teaching was to consider what the father would have done when making decisions, while the broader developmental genealogy independently preserves a paternal teaching pattern centered on responsibility, independence, non-judgment, work, reasons and confronting problems. This pass did not recover an older source preserving the specific decision-rule wording.
findings.source_status: later family/biographical summary; specific earlier wording not independently recovered
what_this_improves: The general paternal-formation context is independently present in the canonical developmental genealogy.
The archive can distinguish the broad father-teaching pattern from the more specific later decision-rule summary.
what_this_does_not_improve: It does not recover the specific childhood wording from an earlier source.
It does not establish that John 5:19 influenced the childhood teaching.
It does not make ordinary parental imitation evidence of a theological Father/Son identity.
findings.next_action: Recover an earlier source for the specific decision-rule wording and date the first explicit John 5:19 comparison separately.
